screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: The History of Concrete
screenings.description: Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

screenings.title: Fjord
screenings.description: From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.title: La Bola Negra
screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: On The Road
screenings.description: ‘Veneno’, a rebellious young drifter, frequents roadside diners where he sleeps with truck drivers. Urgently needing a ride, he meets ‘Muñeco’, a hard-edged driver who keeps to himself. He convinces Muñeco to take him deep into the hyper-masculine world of long-haul trucking across the north of Mexico. As they travel together and an unexpected intimacy builds between them, shadows from Veneno’s past resurface, putting both their lives at risk.

screenings.title: Queen at Sea
screenings.description: Amanda (Academy Award winner Juliette Binoche, The English Patient, The Taste of Things) and her stepfather Martin (Academy Award nominee Tom Courtenay, Doctor Zhivago, 45 Years) struggle with a moral issue that divides them. Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

screenings.title: Wildwood in 35mm
screenings.description: Wildwood is a handcrafted epic fantasy that transports audiences into a secret, dangerously alive world. A girl’s desperate quest to save her baby brother unfolds into a spectacular, high-stakes adventure through a forbidden forest full of enchanted creatures, endearing allies, and formidable adversaries—where an entire hidden realm hangs in the balance. In an era of automation, LAIKA delivers its most ambitious and globally accessible film yet—a bold fusion of human-crafted artistry and cinematic storytelling from the makers of Coraline.

screenings.title: Everest: the Other Side
screenings.director: Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin
screenings.description: EVEREST: THE OTHER SIDE is an intimate portrait of two people bound by love, ambition, and the pursuit of the impossible, from National Geographic Documentary Films and Oscar®-winning filmmakers Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin, directors of FREE SOLO. A thrilling cinematic experience chronicling one of the most dangerous climbs imaginable.

screenings.title: Wicker
screenings.description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
screenings.description: From writer-director Bassam Tariq, YOUR MOTHER YOUR MOTHER YOUR MOTHER stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

screenings.title: The Devils
screenings.description: Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 1-3
screenings.description: “GRIPPING FROM START TO FINISH.” – Sam Adams, Slate CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. A moving tribute to the necessity of resistance.” – Boris Bastide, Le Monde

screenings.description: From Focus Features and Working Title comes an irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles.

screenings.title: The Innkeepers
screenings.description: “This was Ti West’s fourth film with Glass Eye Pix and his follow up to seminal slow-burn THE HOUSE OF THE DEVIL. Ti explained that the crew stayed in the Yankee Peddlar hotel during the shooting of HOUSE and everyone felt it was haunted so he wrote a script for the location. But I know that Ti had pitched the idea of two slacker ghost hunters years before. Look under the hood and you see three ghosts of past present and future in this movie, anticipating West’s newest venture, EBENEZER. And listen for me voicing A CHRISTMAS CAROL off camera on the TV. I’ve been told it’s Scorsese’s favorite Ti West Film.” – Larry Fessenden, producer

screenings.title: Citizen Ruth
screenings.description: U.S., 1996 Directed by Alexander Payne Starring Laura Dern, Swoosie Kurtz, Kelly Preston, Burt Reynolds, Kurtwood Smith, Mary Kay Place, Kenneth Mars, Tippi Hedren Approx. 102 min. Ruth Stoops (Dern), a poor, drug-addled young woman who’s already had four children taken from her by the state, finds herself pregnant again while in jail. When the judge threatens her with a felony charge unless she has an abortion, Ruth is taken in by pro-life activist Gail Stoney (Mary Kay Place), and suddenly becomes the reluctant centerpiece of an escalating tug-of-war between pro-choice and pro-life activists, each eager to use her as a message for their cause. New 4K restoration by IndieCollect, in collaboration with The Criterion Collection and Paramount Pictures A PARAMOUNT PICTURES RELEASE

screenings.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: An Autumn Afternoon
screenings.description: Ozu’s gorgeous 53rd and final feature is a return to a favorite theme, the poignant comedy of marriage, with beloved regular Chishu Ryu as a father giving away his daughter and preparing for another, final goodbye. Good Morning’s satire of creeping consumerism has become more bitter here, the feeling of incoming winter chill is sharper, the entire project imbued with a tang of regret—incidentally, the title literally translates to “The Taste of Autumn Mackerel.”

screenings.title: Edward Scissorhands
screenings.description: On the heels of his Batman bonanza, Burton offered up this Tampa Bay–set modern-day fable of the title’s blade-fingered mechanical man (Johnny Depp), adopted into the suburban home of a family whose daughter (Winona Ryder) becomes the object of his gradually-requited affections. Innocent Edward inadvertently brings trouble to the neighborhood and, finally, the gift of snow on Christmas, in a film that includes the final performance by Vincent Price, and keen insight into pubescent mortification.

screenings.description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. screenings.title: Peppermint Frappé
screenings.description: Chaplin and Saura’s electric creative partnership began with this perverse play on Alfred Hitchcock’s (already quite perverse!) Vertigo, in which meek doctor José Luis López Vázquez becomes besotted with his childhood friend’s bride (Chaplin), and sets about making over a doting assistant (Chaplin, again) at the radiology clinic where he works into the image of the woman he yearns for but cannot have. A delirious and seriously deviant psychological thriller. “I got home quite late and turned on the television; a film in Spanish with subtitles, that I knew absolutely nothing about... It was hard for me to follow and understand but, at the same time, I was convinced it was the film of a great director. I watched the rest of the film glued to the TV set and when it was over I picked up a newspaper and saw that it was Peppermint Frappé.” —Stanley Kubrick

screenings.title: Rushmore
screenings.description: Extracurricular-mad but otherwise unpromising 15-year-old student Max Fisher (Jason Schwartzman) is too busy competing (or so he thinks) with sad sack industrialist Bill Murray for the affections of teacher Olivia Williams to survive “sudden death academic probation” in Anderson’s deeply funny, deeply melancholic—and very class-conscious—sophomore feature. A back-to-school perennial, all dressed up in prep school navy blue and the muted colors of north Texas autumn, positively thrumming with the upstart energy of British Invasion anthems. (“Anderson,” noted admirer Martin Scorsese, “has a fine sense of how music works against an image.”) An irresistible, disarmingly original, delicately wrought comic fable.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Wildwood in 35mm
screenings.description: Wildwood is a handcrafted epic fantasy that transports audiences into a secret, dangerously alive world. A girl’s desperate quest to save her baby brother unfolds into a spectacular, high-stakes adventure through a forbidden forest full of enchanted creatures, endearing allies, and formidable adversaries—where an entire hidden realm hangs in the balance. In an era of automation, LAIKA delivers its most ambitious and globally accessible film yet—a bold fusion of human-crafted artistry and cinematic storytelling from the makers of Coraline.

screenings.title: The Texas Chainsaw Massacre
screenings.description: August 18, 1973. An idyllic Saturday afternoon drive through the Texas hill country becomes a nightmare for five teen-agers when they fall prey to a bizarre, cannibalistic family, and the masked, chainsaw-wielding monster, Leatherface.

screenings.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Citizen Ruth
screenings.description: U.S., 1996 Directed by Alexander Payne Starring Laura Dern, Swoosie Kurtz, Kelly Preston, Burt Reynolds, Kurtwood Smith, Mary Kay Place, Kenneth Mars, Tippi Hedren Approx. 102 min. Ruth Stoops (Dern), a poor, drug-addled young woman who’s already had four children taken from her by the state, finds herself pregnant again while in jail. When the judge threatens her with a felony charge unless she has an abortion, Ruth is taken in by pro-life activist Gail Stoney (Mary Kay Place), and suddenly becomes the reluctant centerpiece of an escalating tug-of-war between pro-choice and pro-life activists, each eager to use her as a message for their cause. New 4K restoration by IndieCollect, in collaboration with The Criterion Collection and Paramount Pictures A PARAMOUNT PICTURES RELEASE

screenings.title: Digger
screenings.description: The most powerful man in the world races to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he unleashed destroys everything.

screenings.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
screenings.description: Dir. Tsai Ming-liang. 2003, 82 mins. DCP. With Lee Kang-sheng, Chen Shiang-chyi, Kiyonobu Mitamura. It’s the last night for a crumbling Fu-Ho movie theater in Taipei, and the film is Dragon Inn (1966), the seminal wuxia by Taiwan-based filmmaker King Hu. The kinetic soundtrack contrasts the theater’s melancholy, slow-moving denizens, including a female box-office attendant with a limp, a cruising Japanese tourist, and two of the stars of Hu’s film. Filled with expertly timed sight gags, Goodbye, Dragon Inn is Tsai’s rueful backwards glance at the disappearance of the filmgoing culture of his youth—and one of the seminal films of the 21st century. With your ticket, request a same-day admission sticker to see Tsai Ming-liang’s It’s a Dream in the Jane Henson Amphitheater. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / $7 MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.description: A story of two married couples — a laid-off worker and his spouse and a documentary filmmaker and her spouse — crossing paths to film a documentary and facing their different lives and hidden desires.

screenings.title: Manhood

Along the way, an OnlyFans star and a father of five put their bodies — and their insecurities — on the line. Blending dark humor with unexpected empathy, MANHOOD examines shame, addiction, and the fragile myths of American masculinity.

Hair-raising deadlines, delirious Bette Davis impressions, and the hostile but exhilarating act of executing a designer’s vision come together in a work that set the bar for all fashion films after.” – Vogue

screenings.title: Cría Cuervos
screenings.description: Taking its title from the Spanish proverb “Raise ravens and they will pick your eyes out,” Saura’s lauded allegorical masterwork, set during the twilight of Spain’s Franco dictatorship, stars Ana Torrent (also seen in Spirit of the Beehive, in the same series) as a traumatized eight-year-old, second of three sisters living with a domineering aunt in Madrid following the death of their parents, who feels herself to be drifting freely between the worlds of the living and the dead and is increasingly convinced she has the ability to snuff out her adult persecutors’ lives. “Both an uncanny drama of family dysfunction and a historical parable of the end of Franco-ism… [Geraldine] Chaplin and Torrent are both outstanding.” —The Guardian

screenings.description: Flaherty’s pioneering ethnographic film depicts the struggle for survival of Inuit hunter Nanook and his family. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

As months pass, while his own family struggles to live with the uncertainty of Chris’s disappearance, Daniel begins helping other families with missing loved ones find answers — and, at times, the closure that continues to elude him.

screenings.title: Society | The Surreal Nightmares of Screaming Mad George
screenings.description: Brian Yuzna’s tangle of class warfare, scatalogy and ugly sex is a stupendously unsubtle eat-the-rich satire. The film’s central metaphor, which suits the 21st century even better than it did the Reagan-Bush 80s, presents the wealthy as literally inhuman gluttons. Since time immemorial, this cupidinous race has parasitically feasted on the inferior homo sapiens during “shuntings,” Burroughsian nightmares of viscera, gobs of lube and denatured flesh. The mutations are the greatest showcase of the unnerving surrealistic makeup designs of Screaming Mad George—which went on to be the primary influence on the make-up designs of films like The Substance and Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil.

screenings.description: Director Manuela Martelli in person! Dir. Manuela Martelli. 2026, 108 min. Chile/United States/Spain/Mexico. DCP. In Spanish, English, and German with English subtitles. Set in 1992 against the backdrop of Chile’s post-Pinochet “economic miracle,” The Meltdown follows nine-year-old Inés during a stay at an Andean ski resort, where she befriends Hanna, a rebellious German teenage athlete. When Hanna suddenly vanishes, Inés is enlisted as a translator in the search, uncovering hidden truths that test her loyalties and hauntingly echo her country’s dark history. In her gripping second feature, which played in competition at this year’s Cannes Un Certain Regard, award-winning director Manuela Martelli (Chile ’76) crafts a tense, atmospheric mystery that uses a child’s perspective to explore complicity, memory, and the lingering shadows of a nation in transition. Chile’s official submission for Best International Feature at the 99th Academy Awards. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / $7 MoMI members. New 4K restoration by IndieCollect, in collaboration with The Criterion Collection and Paramount Pictures A PARAMOUNT PICTURES RELEASE

screenings.title: Nosferatu (with Live Piano Accompaniment)
screenings.description: 35mm with live piano accompaniment by Makia Matsumura Dir. F. W. Murnau. 1922, 94 mins. Germany. 35mm. With Max Schreck, Gustav von Wangenheim, Greta Schröder, Alexander Granach. Groundbreaking German director F. W. Murnau all but invented the horror film for the modern era with this unnerving—and unofficial—adaptation of Bram Stoker’s novel Dracula. Elegant expressionist visuals make this a work of poetic horror, but it’s Schreck’s terrifying makeup and performance that make this film truly unforgettable. Experience Murnau’s silent masterpiece on the big screen with live piano accompaniment. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire
screenings.director: David Greaves Conceived And Filmed By William Greaves

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Tech founder Elizabeth Holmes invites Nathan Fielder to film her before she’s sent to prison.

screenings.title: The Trouble with Harry
screenings.description: The inconvenient corpse, imbued with a sense of tragedy and terror in Hitchcock’s Rope, is the source of borderline-surrealist farce in The Trouble with Harry, his adaptation of Jack Trevor Story’s novel of the same name, a darkly comic tale in which the residents of a small New England hamlet—exteriors were shot on location in Vermont, with the fall foliage radiant in Technicolor—try and repeatedly fail to dispose of a dead body that has appeared in their midst. A rare foray into comedy (albeit of the black variety) for Hitchcock, with Shirley MacLaine, Mildred Natwick, and Jerry “The Beaver” Mathers perfectly embodying a bevy of smalltown American “types.”

screenings.title: Fjord
screenings.description: From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.title: News From Home
screenings.description: Akerman was 26 years old and living in New York City, away from her native Belgium and her mother, when she teamed with DP Babette Mangolte to film this diary/essay/poem in subway stations and on street corners, their images to eventually be paired with Akerman’s recitals of her mother’s fretful letters. Arguably this extraordinary filmmaker’s most perfect and poignant nonfiction work, both one of the greatest portraits of a city ever put on film and a troubling, touching depiction of maternal love. Screens in the English-language version.

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigamtic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

screenings.title: Ec: Man of Aran
screenings.description: Flaherty’s third major film portrays the lives of a family of fisher folk on the Aran Islands off the coast of Galway, Ireland. Flaherty selected the location and subjects because of their isolation as the westernmost outpost of European civilization. In addition, the daily struggle between the islanders and the sea perfectly suited his interests and concerns. The scenes at sea are breathtaking.“His passionate devotion to the portrayal of human gesture and of a man’s fight for his family makes the film an incomparable account of human dignity. Better than anyone, Flaherty knew how to show the true face of Man.” –Georges Sadoul

screenings.title: Occupational Hazard: the First Coral Reefers
screenings.description: OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD: THE FIRST CORAL REEFERS is a feature documentary that journeys back to the 1970s and early 1980s to tell the story of Jimmy Buffett’s original Coral Reefer Band. Set against the creative backdrop of Key West, the film explores the musicians, friendships, touring years, and studio sessions that helped shape Buffett’s legendary sound. Through rare, never-before-seen archival footage and deeply personal interviews with founding members, tour managers, producers and music legends, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD captures the camaraderie, chaos, and magic of an era that thrived on freedom and lived without a rulebook. Narrated by Academy-award winner Jeff Bridges, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD offers fans a deeper look at the people behind the music and the era that helped define Jimmy Buffett’s lasting legacy. This film is a tribute to Buffett and the original Coral Reefers, the places and people that shaped them, the volatile beauty of a musical moment that couldn’t last but changed everything and their candid sentiment toward Buffett. It’s the origin story upon which the Parrot Head empire was built upon, by the people who helped lay the foundation.

screenings.title: Wicker
screenings.description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.title: Halloween
screenings.description: Credited, rightfully, as the film that kickstarted the “slasher” subgenre, Carpenter’s 1978 Halloween is a masterwork of building tension, an exercise in mood and suspense that takes its cues from Hitchcock, unlike most of the 80s gorefests it would inspire. The film’s key innovation – besides the indelibly terrifying image of the blank-faced “shape” aka Michael Myers – is setting it in an innocuous American suburb; there’s nowhere, not even a nice middle class home, where the viewer is safe. Jamie Lee Curtis makes her scream queen debut as one of several babysitters being stalked by a masked, escaped mental patient on Halloween night, her only savior being the patient’s maniacally driven doctor, played with gusto by the great Donald Pleasance. But the secret weapon of Halloween is the score – composed by Carpenter himself – a tinkling, off-meter piano figure that continues to haunt long after the final unsettling frame. A Halloween season perennial.

screenings.title: The History of Concrete
screenings.description: John Wilson (How To with John Wilson) sets out to make the definitive documentary on concrete.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: Harlem Renaissance luminaries discuss their work and legacy during an extraordinary gathering.

screenings.title: The Toxic Avenger
screenings.description: Welcome to Tromaville, New Jersey, a small American town, terrorized by criminals. The town’s corrupt mayor sits idly by while muggers, robbers, and teenage punks victimize helpless citizens. Among the residents of Tromaville is Melvin, a nerdy emaciated janitor at the local health club. That is, until he becomes THE TOXIC AVENGER! A gang of thugs devise a cruel hoax that goes horribly wrong as Melvin is cast through a third story window into a vat of hazardous toxic waste. However, an unexpected metamorphosis takes place. As the chemicals take hold of his body, Melvin turns into the TOXIC AVENGER, doer of good, and brutal mauler of evil! The rest, as they say, is history. See the film that spawned the comic book, website, cartoon, action figures, and three sequels to date! Experience the action that made Troma Entertainment a cinematic legend!CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: An aging pickpocket (John Turturro) has to race against time to avoid a vengeful crime family.

screenings.title: The Innkeepers
screenings.description: “This was Ti West’s fourth film with Glass Eye Pix and his follow up to seminal slow-burn THE HOUSE OF THE DEVIL. Ti explained that the crew stayed in the Yankee Peddlar hotel during the shooting of HOUSE and everyone felt it was haunted so he wrote a script for the location. But I know that Ti had pitched the idea of two slacker ghost hunters years before. Look under the hood and you see three ghosts of past present and future in this movie, anticipating West’s newest venture, EBENEZER. And listen for me voicing A CHRISTMAS CAROL off camera on the TV. I’ve been told it’s Scorsese’s favorite Ti West Film.” – Larry Fessenden, producer

screenings.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: The History of Concrete
screenings.description: Following the finale of his TV show, filmmaker John Wilson searches for a new creative outlet. After attending a workshop on how to write and sell a Hallmark movie, he attempts to apply the same formula to a documentary about concrete.

screenings.title: The Rocky Horror Picture Show: Live Shadow Cast
screenings.description: Starring Tim Curry Susan Sarandon Barry Bostwick Richard O'Brien Patricia Quinn Little Nell Meat Loaf

screenings.title: Possible Love
screenings.description: A story of two married couples — a laid-off worker and his spouse and a documentary filmmaker and her spouse — crossing paths to film a documentary and facing their different lives and hidden desires.

screenings.title: On The Road
screenings.description: ‘Veneno’, a rebellious young drifter, frequents roadside diners where he sleeps with truck drivers. Urgently needing a ride, he meets ‘Muñeco’, a hard-edged driver who keeps to himself. He convinces Muñeco to take him deep into the hyper-masculine world of long-haul trucking across the north of Mexico. As they travel together and an unexpected intimacy builds between them, shadows from Veneno’s past resurface, putting both their lives at risk.

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Thirty-four days before she's sent to prison, notorious Silicon Valley founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move.

screenings.title: La Bola Negra in 35mm
screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: Everest: the Other Side
screenings.director: Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin
screenings.description: EVEREST: THE OTHER SIDE is an intimate portrait of two people bound by love, ambition, and the pursuit of the impossible, from National Geographic Documentary Films and Oscar®-winning filmmakers Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin, directors of FREE SOLO. A thrilling cinematic experience chronicling one of the most dangerous climbs imaginable.

screenings.title: Wild at Heart (new Restoration)
screenings.description: After serving prison time for a self-defense killing, Sailor Ripley (Nicolas Cage) reunites with girlfriend Lula Fortune (Laura Dern). Lula's mother, Marietta (Diane Ladd), desperate to keep them apart, hires a hit man to kill Sailor. But he finds a whole new set of troubles when he and Bobby Peru (Willem Dafoe), an old buddy who's also out to get Sailor, try to rob a store. When Sailor lands in jail yet again, the young lovers appear further than ever from the shared life they covet.

screenings.title: Sense and Sensibility (2026)
screenings.description: From Focus Features and Working Title comes an irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles.

screenings.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
screenings.description: From writer-director Bassam Tariq, YOUR MOTHER YOUR MOTHER YOUR MOTHER stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

screenings.title: Bram Stoker's Dracula
screenings.description: Coppola at his most boldly baroque, Gary Oldman wearing cinema’s most iconic updo, a puppyish young Keanu Reeves trying to make his way back to Winona Ryder, and Anthony Hopkins as vampire hunter Abraham Van Helsing—it’s all here in this opulent production which returns to the original Stoker text and draws out the piercing sexual ache and romantic longing implicit therein.

screenings.title: Wildwood in 35mm
screenings.description: Wildwood is a handcrafted epic fantasy that transports audiences into a secret, dangerously alive world. A girl’s desperate quest to save her baby brother unfolds into a spectacular, high-stakes adventure through a forbidden forest full of enchanted creatures, endearing allies, and formidable adversaries—where an entire hidden realm hangs in the balance. In an era of automation, LAIKA delivers its most ambitious and globally accessible film yet—a bold fusion of human-crafted artistry and cinematic storytelling from the makers of Coraline.

screenings.title: Twilight
screenings.description: A troubled teenage girl moves in with her dad in a small isolated town. She falls for a mysterious loner with a shocking secret; could he have anything to do with the local murders that have started taking place?

screenings.title: The Exorcist
screenings.description: When 12-year-old Regan MacNeil falls ill, she becomes violent and puzzles doctors with the personality of a horrifying entity. Desperate for answers, Regan’s movie-star mother Chris seeks the help of two priests: one who has lost his faith, and an exorcist. Winner of 1973 Oscars for Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Sound Mixing, THE EXORCIST remains one of the most shocking and gripping movies in the history of cinema.

screenings.title: Ju-On: The Grudge
screenings.description: A social worker visits an elderly woman at her house. The woman appears deeply disturbed, but that’s nothing compared to the shapeless black void — also known as “Kayako” — that lurks in an upstairs hallway. Quiet, creepy, and with bursts of unexpected intensity, JU-ON: THE GRUDGE combines liminal spaces and creepypasta chills to rattle your skeleton. There’s nothing scarier than not knowing what’s scaring you.

screenings.title: Grey Gardens
screenings.description: Meet Big and Little Edie Beale: mother and daughter, high-society dropouts, and reclusive cousins of Jackie Onassis. The two manage to thrive together amid the decay and disorder of their East Hampton, New York, mansion, making for an eerily ramshackle echo of the American Camelot. An impossibly intimate portrait, this 1976 documentary by Albert and David Maysles, codirected by Ellen Hovde and Muffie Meyer, quickly became a cult classic and established Little Edie as a fashion icon and philosopher queen.

screenings.title: The Devils
screenings.description: Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

screenings.title: Hellraiser
screenings.description: “We have such sights to show you…” In horror polymath Clive Barker’s adaptation of his novella The Hellbound Heart, horny hedonist Uncle Frank plays with a mysterious puzzle box, summons the Cenobites (led by Doug Bradley in an iconic performance) and endangers his unsuspecting niece (Ashley Laurence). A work of remarkable specificity and imagination, this inimitable, hot and bothered horror landmark is presented in a new 4K restoration.

screenings.title: Queen at Sea
screenings.description: Amanda (Academy Award winner Juliette Binoche, The English Patient, The Taste of Things) and her stepfather Martin (Academy Award nominee Tom Courtenay, Doctor Zhivago, 45 Years) struggle with a moral issue that divides them. Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

screenings.description: In 2006, To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history.

screenings.title: Saturday Afternoon Cartoons: Time for Halloween
screenings.description: Stathes joins Metrograph at the end of October with Time For Halloween, a spooky selection of vintage family-friendly animated shorts to usher in the holiday. Come enjoy a crop of musically inclined skeletons enjoying a midnight graveyard dance; a human artist innocently 'haunting' his cartoon canine companion for a laugh; a little boy telling his younger brother a ghost story by the fireplace; a famous flapper hosting a Halloween house party; and other amusing tales. Spanning the 1920s through the ’50s, this assortment showcases classic characters such as Casper the Friendly Ghost, Popeye, Betty Boop, and others.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: You Can See Everything
screenings.description: Thirty-four days before she’s sent to prison, notorious Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes invites a skeptical film crew to document her every move. What begins as an intimate portrait of an enigamtic felon becomes a mind-bending three-year journey into the abyss.

screenings.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 4-5
screenings.description: “GRIPPING FROM START TO FINISH.” – Sam Adams, Slate CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. A moving tribute to the necessity of resistance.” – Boris Bastide, Le Monde

screenings.title: Fjord (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.title: Digger
screenings.description: The most powerful man in the world races to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he unleashed destroys everything.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
screenings.description: From writer-director Bassam Tariq, YOUR MOTHER YOUR MOTHER YOUR MOTHER stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

screenings.title: I Sell The Dead
screenings.description: “Glenn McQuaid’s movie started out as a low budget period romp but expanded as Glass Eye Pix producer Peter Phok ambitiously attached actors like Dom Monaghan who started working on our movie the day his character’s demise on LOST aired. A lovely cast includes Angus Scrimm from PHANTASM who had become a Glass Eye Regular (AUTOMATONS, SATAN HATES YOU, TALES FROM BEYOND THE PALE) and Glass Eye stalwart John Speredakos (WENDIGO, STRAY BULLETS, CRUMB CATCHER etc). Glenn’s latest film THE RESTORATION OF GRAYSON MANOR is currently in theaters.” – Larry Fessenden, producer, actor

screenings.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Citizen Ruth
screenings.description: U.S., 1996 Directed by Alexander Payne Starring Laura Dern, Swoosie Kurtz, Kelly Preston, Burt Reynolds, Kurtwood Smith, Mary Kay Place, Kenneth Mars, Tippi Hedren Approx. 102 min. Ruth Stoops (Dern), a poor, drug-addled young woman who’s already had four children taken from her by the state, finds herself pregnant again while in jail. When the judge threatens her with a felony charge unless she has an abortion, Ruth is taken in by pro-life activist Gail Stoney (Mary Kay Place), and suddenly becomes the reluctant centerpiece of an escalating tug-of-war between pro-choice and pro-life activists, each eager to use her as a message for their cause. New 4K restoration by IndieCollect, in collaboration with The Criterion Collection and Paramount Pictures A PARAMOUNT PICTURES RELEASE

screenings.title: The Vourdalak
screenings.description: Dir. Adrien Beau. 2023, 90 mins. France, DCP. With Kacey Mottet Klein, Ariane Labed, Grégoire Colin, Vassili Schneider. A genuinely eccentric spin on the vampire story, integrating uncanny puppet effects with its live-action storytelling, this unsettling, lovingly crafted—and often funny—period creep-show adapts “The Family of the Vourdalak,” a novella by Aleksey Konstantinovich Tolstoy written in 1839—that’s nearly 60 years before Bram Stoker’s Dracula. Lost in a misty forest on a royal errand, the foppish Marquis d’Urfé, a diplomatic envoy for the King, happens upon a Serbian family’s home for shelter. Their village ransacked by the Turks, the clan nervously awaits the return of its patriarch, who has been gone six days to fight the enemy; upon his return, he has decidedly transformed into something both more and less than human. Adrien Beau’s ingenious twist on vampire folklore has the genuine feel of a classic horror short story, while its daring marionette effects and widescreen, super 16mm cinematography create a singularly eerie experience. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / $7 MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.description: Amanda (Academy Award winner Juliette Binoche, The English Patient, The Taste of Things) and her stepfather Martin (Academy Award nominee Tom Courtenay, Doctor Zhivago, 45 Years) struggle with a moral issue that divides them. Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

screenings.title: Gentle Monster
screenings.description: Concert pianist Lucy (Léa Seydoux) moves her family to the countryside to help her husband Philip recover from burnout. Their fresh start is shattered by a police visit, leaving Lucy torn between her love for Philip and troubling questions about what he may have done.

screenings.title: The History of Concrete
screenings.description: John Wilson (How To with John Wilson) sets out to make the definitive documentary on concrete.

screenings.title: Wicker
screenings.description: On the outskirts of a village by the sea, lives a Fisherwoman; smelly, single and perpetually ridiculed. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: This haunting doc reveals the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinians.

screenings.title: Primetime
screenings.description: In 2006, To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history.

screenings.title: Closure
screenings.description: After his teenage son, Chris, is last seen by a surveillance camera on a bridge over Warsaw’s turbulent Vistula River, Daniel embarks on an all-consuming search. Armed with self-built boats, drones, and underwater cameras, he relentlessly scours the river’s depths. As months pass, while his own family struggles to live with the uncertainty of Chris’s disappearance, Daniel begins helping other families with missing loved ones find answers — and, at times, the closure that continues to elude him.

screenings.title: Sense and Sensibility (2026)
screenings.description: From Focus Features and Working Title comes an irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: Harlem Renaissance luminaries discuss their work and legacy during an extraordinary gathering.

screenings.title: Everest: the Other Side
screenings.director: Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin
screenings.description: EVEREST: THE OTHER SIDE is an intimate portrait of two people bound by love, ambition, and the pursuit of the impossible, from National Geographic Documentary Films and Oscar®-winning filmmakers Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin, directors of FREE SOLO. A thrilling cinematic experience chronicling one of the most dangerous climbs imaginable.

screenings.title: Wildwood in 35mm
screenings.description: Wildwood is a handcrafted epic fantasy that transports audiences into a secret, dangerously alive world. A girl’s desperate quest to save her baby brother unfolds into a spectacular, high-stakes adventure through a forbidden forest full of enchanted creatures, endearing allies, and formidable adversaries—where an entire hidden realm hangs in the balance. In an era of automation, LAIKA delivers its most ambitious and globally accessible film yet—a bold fusion of human-crafted artistry and cinematic storytelling from the makers of Coraline.

screenings.title: Beetlejuice
screenings.description: With her delivery of the line “My whole life is a dark room… One. Big. Dark. Room,” Winona Ryder cemented herself as a goth girl heroine for the ages, a brooding teen in widow’s weeds relocated by her parents to a creaky country house that happens to be haunted by the unquiet spirits of owners Alec Baldwin and Geena Davis, egged on in mischief-making by Michael Keaton’s Ghost with the Most, whose own hidden motives are rather more malevolent. “A bugaboo farce… Has a kid’s delight in the homegrown surreal… Michael Keaton has never been so uninhibited a comic.”—Pauline Kael, The New Yorker

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

Possible Love
screenings.description: A story of two married couples — a laid-off worker and his spouse and a documentary filmmaker and her spouse — crossing paths to film a documentary and facing their different lives and hidden desires.

screenings.title: Silent Night, Deadly Night 5: The Toy Maker | The Surreal Nightmares of Screaming Mad George
screenings.description: The series curator’s dark horse pick for must-see movie in the Screaming Mad George retrospective, the late entry from the direct-to-video years of the long, byzantine Christmas series is shockingly entertaining. The story involves a young boy who is traumatized when bizarre mystery toys kill people including his deadbeat father, his school bully, and a landlord (yes!) in strange and gruesome ways. This puts him in touch with a toy seller named Joe Petto—owner of “Petto’s Toys” (say it out loud)—played by a typically unhinged late-career Mickey Rooney. And from there, the story takes a twist into being a… Terminator knock-off? To the best of our knowledge, Silent Night, Deadly Night 5: The Toy Maker has never screened theatrically in New York City on 35mm.

screenings.title: Occupational Hazard: the First Coral Reefers
screenings.description: OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD: THE FIRST CORAL REEFERS is a feature documentary that journeys back to the 1970s and early 1980s to tell the story of Jimmy Buffett’s original Coral Reefer Band. Set against the creative backdrop of Key West, the film explores the musicians, friendships, touring years, and studio sessions that helped shape Buffett’s legendary sound. Through rare, never-before-seen archival footage and deeply personal interviews with founding members, tour managers, producers and music legends, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD captures the camaraderie, chaos, and magic of an era that thrived on freedom and lived without a rulebook. Narrated by Academy-award winner Jeff Bridges, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD offers fans a deeper look at the people behind the music and the era that helped define Jimmy Buffett’s lasting legacy. This film is a tribute to Buffett and the original Coral Reefers, the places and people that shaped them, the volatile beauty of a musical moment that couldn’t last but changed everything and their candid sentiment toward Buffett. It’s the origin story upon which the Parrot Head empire was built upon, by the people who helped lay the foundation.

screenings.title: La Bola Negra in 35mm
screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: On The Road
screenings.description: ‘Veneno’, a rebellious young drifter, frequents roadside diners where he sleeps with truck drivers. Urgently needing a ride, he meets ‘Muñeco’, a hard-edged driver who keeps to himself. He convinces Muñeco to take him deep into the hyper-masculine world of long-haul trucking across the north of Mexico. As they travel together and an unexpected intimacy builds between them, shadows from Veneno’s past resurface, putting both their lives at risk.

screenings.title: The Exorcist
screenings.description: Please note: due to the deteriorated condition of the 35mm print we received, this screening will now be projected in 4K DCP. Dir. William Friedkin. 1973, 122 mins. U.S. 4K DCP. With Ellen Burstyn, Linda Blair, Jason Miller, Max von Sydow. Widely considered one of the scariest films ever made, The Exorcist has shocked and fascinated generations of viewers. Directed by William Friedkin and written by William Peter Blatty, adapting his own best-selling 1971 novel, the film made an essential contribution to the horror genre, pitting the Catholic church against a demon for control of a young girl’s soul. The film’s remarkable, often shocking effects were done by the brilliant and pioneering makeup master Dick Smith (Little Big Man, The Godfather), who transformed the possessed young girl Regan (Linda Blair) into a foul, blasphemous monster. Nominated for ten Academy Awards, including Best Picture, and winning for Best Adapted Screenplay and Best Sound. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Purchase tickets for October 24 at 3:00 p.m. Purchase tickets for October 31 at 3:30 p.m. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Vera
screenings.description: “When Caden Mark Gardner and I co-curated Vera as part of the original Masc series in 2022, Caden did some amazing research on the film. Together we determined that it is one of the earliest (and also one of the best) portrayals in world cinema of a transmasculine character. And the film’s protagonist, Bauer (the film’s title is his dead name), shines through as an incredible transmasc hero. As he confidently proclaims to the powers that be, ‘I’m not what everyone thinks I am. You hear me? I’m different. I’m something else. Something else.’” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist

screenings.title: The History of Concrete

In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. screenings.title: Sense and Sensibility (2026)

screenings.title: Ec: Hollis Frampton
screenings.description: ZORNS LEMMA(1970, 60 min, 16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives.)“A major poetic work. Created and put together by a very clear eye-head, this original and complex abstract work moves beyond the letters of the alphabet, beyond words and beyond Freud. If you don’t understand it the first time you see it, don’t despair, see it again! When you finally ‘get it,’ a small light, possibly a candle, will light itself inside your forehead.” –Ernie Gehr&HAPAX LEGOMENA I: (nostalgia)(1971, 36 min, 16mm. Preserved by Anthology Film Archives, MoMA, and the NYU Moving Image Archiving and Preservation Program, with funding from the National Film Preservation Foundation.)“In (nostalgia) the time it takes for a photograph to burn (and thus confirm its two-dimensionality) becomes the clock within the film, while Frampton plays the critic, asynchronously glossing, explicating, narrating, mythologizing his earlier art, and his earlier life, as he commits them both to the fire of a labyrinthine structure; for Borges too was one of his earlier masters, and he grins behind the facades of logic, mathematics, and physical demonstrations which are the formal metaphors for most of Frampton’s films.” –P. Adams SitneyTotal running time: ca. 100 min.CLICK HERE TO BOOK TICKETS NOW!

screenings.title: The Trouble with Harry
screenings.description: The inconvenient corpse, imbued with a sense of tragedy and terror in Hitchcock’s Rope, is the source of borderline-surrealist farce in The Trouble with Harry, his adaptation of Jack Trevor Story’s novel of the same name, a darkly comic tale in which the residents of a small New England hamlet—exteriors were shot on location in Vermont, with the fall foliage radiant in Technicolor—try and repeatedly fail to dispose of a dead body that has appeared in their midst. A rare foray into comedy (albeit of the black variety) for Hitchcock, with Shirley MacLaine, Mildred Natwick, and Jerry “The Beaver” Mathers perfectly embodying a bevy of smalltown American “types.”

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Citizen Ruth

Ruth Stoops (Dern), a poor, drug-addled young woman who’s already had four children taken from her by the state, finds herself pregnant again while in jail. When the judge threatens her with a felony charge unless she has an abortion, Ruth is taken in by pro-life activist Gail Stoney (Mary Kay Place), and suddenly becomes the reluctant centerpiece of an escalating tug-of-war between pro-choice and pro-life activists, each eager to use her as a message for their cause. screenings.title: The Brides of Dracula

After cherubic five-year-old Carol Anne Freeling is abducted by malevolent spirits, her parents are determined to bring her back at any cost. screenings.description: Both the pinnacle of his career and the giallo subgenre, Dario Argento’s Suspiria ranks in the pantheon of the greatest horror movies of all time, and with damn good reason. It all adds up to that rare witches brew: the perfect horror experience.

screenings.title: Halloween
screenings.description: Credited, rightfully, as the film that kickstarted the “slasher” subgenre, Carpenter’s 1978 Halloween is a masterwork of building tension, an exercise in mood and suspense that takes its cues from Hitchcock, unlike most of the 80s gorefests it would inspire. The film’s key innovation – besides the indelibly terrifying image of the blank-faced “shape” aka Michael Myers – is setting it in an innocuous American suburb; there’s nowhere, not even a nice middle class home, where the viewer is safe. Jamie Lee Curtis makes her scream queen debut as one of several babysitters being stalked by a masked, escaped mental patient on Halloween night, her only savior being the patient’s maniacally driven doctor, played with gusto by the great Donald Pleasance. But the secret weapon of Halloween is the score – composed by Carpenter himself – a tinkling, off-meter piano figure that continues to haunt long after the final unsettling frame. A Halloween season perennial.
