screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.description: “Alferd Packer, awaiting his execution on the charge of cannibalism, recounts his harrowing story of survival in the snow-covered Colorado mountains while on an ill-fated quest for riches. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. screenings.title: Blade Runner: The Final Cut

Working from a novel by cult writer Philip K. Dick to create a film that would become the gold standard for sci-fi noir, director Scott shares credit here with “visual futurist” Syd Mead’s design concepts and synth pioneer Vangelis’s atmospheric score.

The Shining: International Version + Garrett Brown and Michael Chaiken in person
screenings.description: U.S. Theatrical Premiere Preceded by a conversation with Steadicam inventor Garrett Brown and archivist Michael Chaiken Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1980. 114 mins. U.S. 4K DCP. With Jack Nicholson, Shelley Duvall, Scatman Crothers, Danny Loyd. When The Shining was first released in 1980, most critics were generally baffled or negative, unable to understand Stanley Kubrick’s visionary approach to the horror genre, which prioritized deliberate pacing, deferred catharsis, and haunting abstract imagery. Today, we see, of course, that Kubrick was laying the groundwork for future generations of aspiring art-horror filmmakers. But in the moment, Kubrick responded to the critiques by editing a shorter version with less slack for the European market, a tinkered cut that he called “The Two-Hour Version.” Shining obsessive and Pixar animator Lee Unkrich—writer of the Taschen book Stanley Kubrick’s The Shining—notes that Kubrick’s long-time assistant Leon Vitali claimed this was Kubrick’s preferred cut. Decide for yourself in this rare opportunity to see the International Version on the big screen, followed by a screening of the original U.S. cut. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Primetime
screenings.description: In 2006, To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen sets out to make television history.

screenings.title: Fjord (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.title: The Last Winter
screenings.description: “This was conceived as a sequel of sorts to my family drama WENDIGO, expanding the themes of cultural cannibalism to themes of Manifest Destiny and climate collapse, all of which relate to the Wendigo Mythology of Ojibway origins. It was my biggest budget and my biggest cast and premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival and was bought by IFC to some fanfare. It’s in the permanent collection at MOMA. It continues my focus on the left right political divide that makes solving problems impossible.” – Larry Fessenden, director

screenings.title: Citizen Ruth
screenings.description: U.S., 1996 Directed by Alexander Payne Starring Laura Dern, Swoosie Kurtz, Kelly Preston, Burt Reynolds, Kurtwood Smith, Mary Kay Place, Kenneth Mars, Tippi Hedren Approx. 102 min. Ruth Stoops (Dern), a poor, drug-addled young woman who’s already had four children taken from her by the state, finds herself pregnant again while in jail. When the judge threatens her with a felony charge unless she has an abortion, Ruth is taken in by pro-life activist Gail Stoney (Mary Kay Place), and suddenly becomes the reluctant centerpiece of an escalating tug-of-war between pro-choice and pro-life activists, each eager to use her as a message for their cause. New 4K restoration by IndieCollect, in collaboration with The Criterion Collection and Paramount Pictures A PARAMOUNT PICTURES RELEASE

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: An aging pickpocket (John Turturro) has to race against time to avoid a vengeful crime family.

screenings.description: Amanda (Academy Award winner Juliette Binoche, The English Patient, The Taste of Things) and her stepfather Martin (Academy Award nominee Tom Courtenay, Doctor Zhivago, 45 Years) struggle with a moral issue that divides them. Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

screenings.title: Wild at Heart (new Restoration)
screenings.description: After serving prison time for a self-defense killing, Sailor Ripley (Nicolas Cage) reunites with girlfriend Lula Fortune (Laura Dern). Lula's mother, Marietta (Diane Ladd), desperate to keep them apart, hires a hit man to kill Sailor. But he finds a whole new set of troubles when he and Bobby Peru (Willem Dafoe), an old buddy who's also out to get Sailor, try to rob a store. When Sailor lands in jail yet again, the young lovers appear further than ever from the shared life they covet.

screenings.title: Gentle Monster
screenings.description: Concert pianist Lucy (Léa Seydoux) moves her family to the countryside to help her husband Philip recover from burnout. Their fresh start is shattered by a police visit, leaving Lucy torn between her love for Philip and troubling questions about what he may have done.

screenings.title: Ken Russell’s The Devils
screenings.description: See the uncut and unfiltered theatrical experience Ken Russell envisioned for his 1971 classic.

One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: This haunting doc reveals the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinians.

screenings.title: All That Heaven Allows
screenings.description: Perhaps the very finest of Sirk’s Ross Hunter-produced melodramas, All That Heaven Allows pairs Jane Wyman and Rock Hudson as, respectively, a well-off widow in country club Connecticut, and the broad-necked, Thoreau-reading gardener who she falls for. Her priggish children, aghast, conspire to break off the pairing, an endeavor that ends in a bone-chilling Christmas conciliation—the presentation of a gift television set as a kind of death sentence. Of this scene Rainer Werner Fassbinder, profoundly marked by his encounter with Sirk’s film, would write: “At that point everyone in the moviehouse breaks down. They suddenly understand something about the world and what it does to people.” Right on.

screenings.title: Closure
screenings.description: After his teenage son, Chris, is last seen by a surveillance camera on a bridge over Warsaw’s turbulent Vistula River, Daniel embarks on an all-consuming search. Armed with self-built boats, drones, and underwater cameras, he relentlessly scours the river’s depths. As months pass, while his own family struggles to live with the uncertainty of Chris’s disappearance, Daniel begins helping other families with missing loved ones find answers — and, at times, the closure that continues to elude him.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: Harlem Renaissance luminaries discuss their work and legacy during an extraordinary gathering.

screenings.title: Everest: the Other Side
screenings.director: Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin
screenings.description: EVEREST: THE OTHER SIDE is an intimate portrait of two people bound by love, ambition, and the pursuit of the impossible, from National Geographic Documentary Films and Oscar®-winning filmmakers Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin, directors of FREE SOLO. A thrilling cinematic experience chronicling one of the most dangerous climbs imaginable.

screenings.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Wildwood in 35mm
screenings.description: Wildwood is a handcrafted epic fantasy that transports audiences into a secret, dangerously alive world. A girl’s desperate quest to save her baby brother unfolds into a spectacular, high-stakes adventure through a forbidden forest full of enchanted creatures, endearing allies, and formidable adversaries—where an entire hidden realm hangs in the balance. In an era of automation, LAIKA delivers its most ambitious and globally accessible film yet—a bold fusion of human-crafted artistry and cinematic storytelling from the makers of Coraline.

screenings.title: Sense and Sensibility (2026)
screenings.description: From Focus Features and Working Title comes an irresistible new take on Jane Austen’s iconic Sense and Sensibility: a charming, witty, and deeply relatable story of love and sisterhood starring Daisy Edgar-Jones and Esmé Creed-Miles.

screenings.description: One of the quintessential early-’90s cult films, Freaked was adapted by Alex Winter and Tom Stern from their psychotronic MTV series The Idiot Box. Winter plays a vain Hollywood actor who takes a gig promoting an evil South African fertilizer company. But an airplane incident lands him in the middle of a grotesque amusement park, where he is transformed into a member of its expansive freak show. A deliriously grotesque live-action cartoon, Freaked is a carnivalesque melange of eye-popping make-up effects and fun-house set design. It also features an all-star cameo casting ranging from Gibby Haynes of The Butthole Surfers to Mr. T, plus masked appearances from Keanu Reeves and future Wicked director Jon M. Chu. Must be seen to be believed.

screenings.title: Occupational Hazard: the First Coral Reefers
screenings.description: OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD: THE FIRST CORAL REEFERS is a feature documentary that journeys back to the 1970s and early 1980s to tell the story of Jimmy Buffett’s original Coral Reefer Band. Set against the creative backdrop of Key West, the film explores the musicians, friendships, touring years, and studio sessions that helped shape Buffett’s legendary sound. Through rare, never-before-seen archival footage and deeply personal interviews with founding members, tour managers, producers and music legends, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD captures the camaraderie, chaos, and magic of an era that thrived on freedom and lived without a rulebook. Narrated by Academy-award winner Jeff Bridges, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD offers fans a deeper look at the people behind the music and the era that helped define Jimmy Buffett’s lasting legacy. This film is a tribute to Buffett and the original Coral Reefers, the places and people that shaped them, the volatile beauty of a musical moment that couldn’t last but changed everything and their candid sentiment toward Buffett. It’s the origin story upon which the Parrot Head empire was built upon, by the people who helped lay the foundation.

screenings.title: La Bola Negra in 35mm
screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

Urgently needing a ride, he meets ‘Muñeco’, a hard-edged driver who keeps to himself. He convinces Muñeco to take him deep into the hyper-masculine world of long-haul trucking across the north of Mexico. As they travel together and an unexpected intimacy builds between them, shadows from Veneno’s past resurface, putting both their lives at risk.

screenings.title: Far From Heaven
screenings.description: An homage to the Eisenhower era melodramas of Douglas Sirk that reworks the basic materials of his 1955 All That Heaven Allows to explicitly explore dynamics of sexual and social transgression verboten in the Hollywood of Sirk’s time, Haynes’s sumptuous film—featuring a period-appropriate score by Elmer Bernstein and a remarkable approximation of Technicolor saturation by cinematographer Ed Lachman—stars Julianne Moore and Dennis Quaid as a well-heeled Connecticut couple whose seemingly perfect suburban existence is upended when he’s discovered trawling Hartford’s gay bars and she strikes up an affair with her new Black gardener, played with compassionate gravity by Dennis Haysbert.

screenings.title: The Shining
screenings.description: Dir. Stanley Kubrick. 1980. 144 mins. U.S. 4K DCP. With Jack Nicholson, Shelley Duvall, Scatman Crothers, Danny Loyd. Rivers of blood spew from an elevator. The ghosts of two girls beckon in a hallway. An axe blasts through a bathroom wall to get at the terrified woman inside. With remarkable performances by Jack Nicholson and Shelley Duvall, iconic set design, and groundbreaking Steadicam photography, Kubrick’s masterpiece of transcendent horror adapts Stephen King’s novel about Jack Torrance, an alcoholic writer driven mad while working as the caretaker of the cavernous Colorado hotel the Overlook over the course of one isolated winter. Simply put, this is one of the most aesthetically influential films ever made. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / $7 MoMI members. screenings.description: Flirting with the conventions of blaxploitation and horror, Bill Gunn’s revolutionary independent film Ganja & Hess is a highly stylized and utterly original treatise on sex, religion, and African American identity. Duane Jones (Night of the Living Dead) stars as anthropologist Hess Green, who is stabbed with an ancient ceremonial dagger by his unstable assistant (director Bill Gunn), bestowing upon him the blessing of immortality… and the curse of an unquenchable thirst for blood. When the assistant’s beautiful and outspoken wife Ganja (Marlene Clark) comes searching for her missing husband, she and Hess form an unexpected partnership. Together, they explore just how much power blood holds.

screenings.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: News from Home + Interior NY Subway, 14th Street

Arguably this extraordinary filmmaker’s most perfect and poignant nonfiction work, both one of the greatest portraits of a city ever put on film and a troubling, touching depiction of maternal love. screenings.title: The Hound of the Baskervilles

With the invaluable assistance of Jack Asher’s subdued Technicolor photography, Fisher wrings every drop of atmosphere out of Doyle’s tale of mist-shrouded moors and ancestral curses, making this one of Holmes’s very finest big-screen outings. (Special mention is due to Fisher’s ingenious use of child stand-ins for his leads to establish the terrible proportions of the eponymous mastiff.)

screenings.title: Naza

screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 1-3
screenings.description: “GRIPPING FROM START TO FINISH.” – Sam Adams, Slate CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Occupational Hazard: the First Coral Reefers
screenings.description: OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD: THE FIRST CORAL REEFERS is a feature documentary that journeys back to the 1970s and early 1980s to tell the story of Jimmy Buffett’s original Coral Reefer Band. Set against the creative backdrop of Key West, the film explores the musicians, friendships, touring years, and studio sessions that helped shape Buffett’s legendary sound. Through rare, never-before-seen archival footage and deeply personal interviews with founding members, tour managers, producers and music legends, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD captures the camaraderie, chaos, and magic of an era that thrived on freedom and lived without a rulebook. Narrated by Academy-award winner Jeff Bridges, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD offers fans a deeper look at the people behind the music and the era that helped define Jimmy Buffett’s lasting legacy. This film is a tribute to Buffett and the original Coral Reefers, the places and people that shaped them, the volatile beauty of a musical moment that couldn’t last but changed everything and their candid sentiment toward Buffett. It’s the origin story upon which the Parrot Head empire was built upon, by the people who helped lay the foundation.

Reuniting stars Jeffrey Combs as Dr. Herbert West and Bruce Abbott as former medical student Dr. Dan Cain, Bride sees the duo expand their experiments to re-animating individual severed limbs. Their goal: to resurrect Cain’s fiance by cobbling pieces of other women around her preserved heart. And from there, the creations only get crazier. Bride of Re-Animator is an extraordinary follow-up to Brian Yuzna and Screaming Mad George’s previous collaboration Society with an all-star special effects team also includes John Carl Buechler and the KNB EFX Group.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Yi Yi
screenings.description: The last work of a master filmmaker who died far too young, the gentle, restrained, and terribly humane Yi Yi observes the interplay between three generations of an upper middle-class Taipei family. Comic when dealing in the foibles of its excellent ensemble cast and the mores of the urban bourgeoise, yet also possessed throughout by an air of unmistakable melancholy and lingering regret at missed opportunities, this feeling made all the deeper when one considers the great films Yang might still have produced. A work of epic length that avoids even a hint of bombast, dedicated instead to working its way into the hidden, niche spaces of everyday people’s emotional lives, it’s a film as rich and as sad as life itself.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: The Mad Songs of Fernanda Hussein
screenings.description: Boston-based filmmaker and former Harvard Film Archive curator John Gianvito had made a few films before the 20th century became the 21st, but he would wind up emerging as one of the definitive filmmakers of the current century during its first decade. His six years of work on Gulf War I cri de cœur The Mad Songs of Fernanda Hussein wound up serving as one of the definitive commentaries on the upcoming century when it premiered in 2001. Mad Songs served as a work of inadvertent commentary on the bloodlust spurred by the Twin Tower attacks, and the Gulf War II that was going to come about as a result. It was also a work of intensely personal cinephilia-inspired curation: Griffith- and Wyler-adjacent structuring of multiple war-at-home storylines was melded with archival footage and performance documentary, resulting in a bold and sprawling hybrid work. Despite fierce advocacy from notable champions in Chantal Akerman, Peter Watkins, Jonathan Rosenbaum, and Dennis Lim, it was not an easy film to see in 2001 and it has not gotten much easier since. He’d take another six years to make his next film, this time decidedly aimed at the domestic. Profit Motive and the Whispering Wind (2007) was a film whose more minimalist scale and running time didn’t reduce its power. Its simultaneously rousing and despairing analysis, courtesy of Howard Zinn, marked a turn towards a more domestic issue: how America eats its rabble rousers but leaves a tribute to them later. The groundwork laid by the champions of Mad Songs resulted in Profit Motive finding more of an audience, and it subsequently being named the Best Experimental Film of 2007 by the National Society of Film Critics.

screenings.title: Occupational Hazard: the First Coral Reefers
screenings.description: OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD: THE FIRST CORAL REEFERS is a feature documentary that journeys back to the 1970s and early 1980s to tell the story of Jimmy Buffett’s original Coral Reefer Band. Set against the creative backdrop of Key West, the film explores the musicians, friendships, touring years, and studio sessions that helped shape Buffett’s legendary sound. Through rare, never-before-seen archival footage and deeply personal interviews with founding members, tour managers, producers and music legends, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD captures the camaraderie, chaos, and magic of an era that thrived on freedom and lived without a rulebook. Narrated by Academy-award winner Jeff Bridges, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD offers fans a deeper look at the people behind the music and the era that helped define Jimmy Buffett’s lasting legacy. This film is a tribute to Buffett and the original Coral Reefers, the places and people that shaped them, the volatile beauty of a musical moment that couldn’t last but changed everything and their candid sentiment toward Buffett. It’s the origin story upon which the Parrot Head empire was built upon, by the people who helped lay the foundation.

Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.description: MANHOOD follows Dallas entrepreneur Bill Moore as he attempts to make penis enlargement as commonplace as Botox. Along the way, an OnlyFans star and a father of five put their bodies — and their insecurities — on the line. Blending dark humor with unexpected empathy, MANHOOD examines shame, addiction, and the fragile myths of American masculinity.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: All That Heaven Allows
screenings.description: Perhaps the very finest of Sirk’s Ross Hunter-produced melodramas, All That Heaven Allows pairs Jane Wyman and Rock Hudson as, respectively, a well-off widow in country club Connecticut, and the broad-necked, Thoreau-reading gardener who she falls for. Her priggish children, aghast, conspire to break off the pairing, an endeavor that ends in a bone-chilling Christmas conciliation—the presentation of a gift television set as a kind of death sentence. Of this scene Rainer Werner Fassbinder, profoundly marked by his encounter with Sirk’s film, would write: “At that point everyone in the moviehouse breaks down. They suddenly understand something about the world and what it does to people.” Right on.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.description: Concert pianist Lucy (Léa Seydoux) moves her family to the countryside to help her husband Philip recover from burnout. Their fresh start is shattered by a police visit, leaving Lucy torn between her love for Philip and troubling questions about what he may have done.

screenings.title: Birds of War
screenings.description: Spanning 13 years of revolution, war and exile, from besieged Aleppo to the confines of a London newsroom, Lebanese journalist Janay Boulos and Syrian activist and cameraman Abd Alkader Habak relive their war reporting and their unexpected love story, using a vast personal trove of archives.

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

Has Amanda’s mother Leslie (Anna Calder-Marshall) who is suffering from advanced dementia, lost the ability to make critical decisions in her own best interests? And, if so, who is responsible – a spouse, a child, an institution – for making such a determination? As Amanda and Martin are forced to make increasingly difficult choices, the repercussions spiral out of their control.

screenings.title: Bored Teenagers

The follow-up to this authentic document of youth culture was the ZDF production BORED TEENAGERS, part of the “Das kleine Fernsehspiel” series; it was filmed in 1979 in the wake of the RAF panic – wanted posters are visible in the background several times throughout the film. The movie blends concert footage of the English punk band The Adverts with a loose narrative thread about a young punk named Peter and his hairdresser girlfriend, Karin, as they follow the band – led by TV Smith and Gaye Advert – on their tour through Germany. It is an entertaining yet quirky journey through a late-70s musical subculture.” –OX-FANZINECLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

A thrilling cinematic experience chronicling one of the most dangerous climbs imaginable.

screenings.title: Gentlemen Prefer Blondes
screenings.description: Lorelei Lee (Marilyn Monroe) is a beautiful showgirl engaged to be married to the wealthy Gus Esmond (Tommy Noonan), much to the disapproval of Gus' rich father, Esmond Sr., who thinks that Lorelei is just after his money. When Lorelei goes on a cruise accompanied only by her best friend, Dorothy Shaw (Jane Russell), Esmond Sr. hires Ernie Malone (Elliott Reid), a private detective, to follow her and report any questionable behavior that would disqualify her from the marriage.

screenings.title: Occupational Hazard: the First Coral Reefers
screenings.description: OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD: THE FIRST CORAL REEFERS is a feature documentary that journeys back to the 1970s and early 1980s to tell the story of Jimmy Buffett’s original Coral Reefer Band. Set against the creative backdrop of Key West, the film explores the musicians, friendships, touring years, and studio sessions that helped shape Buffett’s legendary sound. Through rare, never-before-seen archival footage and deeply personal interviews with founding members, tour managers, producers and music legends, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD captures the camaraderie, chaos, and magic of an era that thrived on freedom and lived without a rulebook. Narrated by Academy-award winner Jeff Bridges, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD offers fans a deeper look at the people behind the music and the era that helped define Jimmy Buffett’s lasting legacy. This film is a tribute to Buffett and the original Coral Reefers, the places and people that shaped them, the volatile beauty of a musical moment that couldn’t last but changed everything and their candid sentiment toward Buffett. It’s the origin story upon which the Parrot Head empire was built upon, by the people who helped lay the foundation.

screenings.title: Wildwood in 35mm

A girl’s desperate quest to save her baby brother unfolds into a spectacular, high-stakes adventure through a forbidden forest full of enchanted creatures, endearing allies, and formidable adversaries—where an entire hidden realm hangs in the balance. In an era of automation, LAIKA delivers its most ambitious and globally accessible film yet—a bold fusion of human-crafted artistry and cinematic storytelling from the makers of Coraline.

screenings.title: Strangers on a Train
screenings.description: “Criss cross.” Hitchcock’s adaptation of Highsmith’s 1951 page-turner kicks off with a casual encounter that reads like a same-sex pickup, as tennis star Guy Haines (Farley Granger) inadvertently agrees to “swap murders” with preening rich kid Bruno Anthony (Robert Walker, in a career performance), and continues through some of the finest set pieces of Hitch’s career: a tennis match at Forest Hills, Bruno stalking his prey through a vulgar county fair, and an out-of-control carousel.

Urgently needing a ride, he meets ‘Muñeco’, a hard-edged driver who keeps to himself. He convinces Muñeco to take him deep into the hyper-masculine world of long-haul trucking across the north of Mexico. As they travel together and an unexpected intimacy builds between them, shadows from Veneno’s past resurface, putting both their lives at risk.

screenings.title: Electra, My Love
screenings.description: Jancsó’s radically original, downright hypnotic retelling of the Ancient Greek myth against the backdrop of the puszta, Hungary’s vast, muddy plains, is among the long-take master’s most bravura stylistic performances, its 70-minute runtime made up of only twelve intricately composed shots. Reworking the tale of Electra and her ill use at the hands of Aegisthus—the man who loved her mother and murdered her father 15 years ago—Jancsó produces a timeless meditation on tyranny and rebellion—and a resounding call to resistance.

screenings.title: Possible Love
screenings.description: A story of two married couples — a laid-off worker and his spouse and a documentary filmmaker and her spouse — crossing paths to film a documentary and facing their different lives and hidden desires.

screenings.title: The Devils

The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

Winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes and an international pop phenomenon, Oldboy was a revenge thriller unlike any that had come before, featuring passages of pure bravura filmmaking (that one-shot hallway donnybrook!) and surreal sicko humor that’ll put you off of sushi for a while. “Put together with brutally uncompromising style [and] the cold-steel edge of a knife against your throat. A dark and thrillingly horrible adventure into the realms of the unthinkable.” —The Guardian

It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Fatherland
screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... Told with exacting restraint yet as layered as the lacquer on an ebony Biedermeier console, this forms a loose triptych with Pawlikowski’s last two features, IDA and COLD WAR, both of which were set at least partly behind the Iron Curtain... It is immaculately performed by Zischler and especially Hüller, grounding the film throughout with an uncanny, expressive stillness. But it is also exquisitely rendered in the same boxy ratio and silvery monochrome lensing Pawlikowski and DP Lukasz Zal (THE ZONE OF INTEREST) deployed on IDA and COLD WAR, and scrupulously detailed down to the ruined buildings, sharply cut suits, surly restaurant service and eclectic selection of jazz, classical and folk tunes chosen by Pawlikowski, all of which is sure to set discriminating viewers swooning.” – Leslie Felperin, The Hollywood Reporter

screenings.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 4-5
screenings.description: “GRIPPING FROM START TO FINISH.” – Sam Adams, Slate CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. A moving tribute to the necessity of resistance.” – Boris Bastide, Le Monde

screenings.description: From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.title: Who Killed Alex Odeh?
screenings.description: In October 1985, Santa Ana, California was shaken by a brazen act of political violence when Palestinian American Alex Odeh, a beloved teacher and community leader, was killed by a tripwire bomb planted in his office. Despite substantial evidence and identified suspects, the case was never solved. Who Killed Alex Odeh? reopens the mystery, tracking a renewed investigation in real time as new leads emerge, long-buried records come to light, and the forces behind a political assassination are finally confronted. In English, Arabic and Hebrew with English subtitles.

screenings.description: ★★★★★ “Another expansive, enriching work from a modern master.” – Phil de Semlyen, Time Out “A perfectly cut jewel of a movie... The power of the movie creeps up on you with its emotional restraint, the beauty of its black-and-white images and the delicacy with which Pawlikowski explores the devastations trembling under the faces of both father and daughter...” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “Stunning... an exquisite study of family, identity, and art where future ideals are intertwined with historical remorse.” – Tomris Laffly, Elle “[A] damn-near perfect period piece... screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Visible Humans
screenings.description: With artist and ophthalmologist Benjamin Freeman and curator Elisabeth Sherman in person The Visible Human Project began in the late 1990s with sponsorship from the National Library of Medicine. Its aim was to make a complete 3D rendering of the human body for educational use. Now in the public domain, these images raise questions about consent and normative ideals. This evening will interrogate this project and feature a screening of the short film Visible Woman, which is included in our exhibition Overexposed; a presentation by ophthalmologist and photographer Benjamin Freeman; and a discussion including curator Elisabeth Sherman. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission. Special Guests: Elisabeth Sherman is the Robert A. and Elizabeth Rohn Jeffe Chief Curator and Deputy Director at the Museum of the City of New York. Previously, she was Chief Curator and Director of Curatorial Affairs at the International Center of Photography (ICP). Prior to ICP, she was a curator at the Whitney Museum of American Art, where she organized and co-organized many critically acclaimed exhibitions including Dawoud Bey: An American Project, Zoe Leonard: Survey, and Making Knowing: Craft in Art, 1960-2019. At ICP she curated, among others, Naima Green: Instead, I Spin Fantasies, Sheida Soleimani: Panjereh, Yto Barrada: Part Time Abstractionist, and ICP at 50. She is co-editor of the catalog Overexposed: Art, Technology, and the Body. Benji Freeman is a photographer and physician based in New York City. His photography draws from medical epistemologies, techniques, and image archives, investigating the modern aesthetics of caring for others as the actual work of healthcare becomes increasingly automatable. He has taught workshops on photographic technique, the visual culture of medicine, and the anatomy of the visual system, and he has written about the role of photographic perception in medical education. He is currently an ophthalmology resident at Columbia University Medical Center.

screenings.description: Set in a richly exaggerated 17th-century England, Peter Greenaway’s sumptuous and sensuously charged brainteaser catapulted him to the forefront of international art cinema. Adorned with intricate wordplay, extravagant costumes and opulent photography, Greenaway’s first narrative feature weaves a labyrinthine mystery around the maxim “draw what you see, not what you know.” An aristocratic wife (Janet Suzman) commissions a young, cocksure draughtsman (Anthony Higgins) to sketch her husband’s property while he is away—in exchange for a fee, room and board, and one sexual favor for each of the twelve drawings. As the draughtsman becomes more entrenched in the devious schemings in this seemingly idyllic country home, curious details emerge in his drawings that may reveal a murder.

screenings.title: Occupational Hazard: the First Coral Reefers
screenings.description: OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD: THE FIRST CORAL REEFERS is a feature documentary that journeys back to the 1970s and early 1980s to tell the story of Jimmy Buffett’s original Coral Reefer Band. Set against the creative backdrop of Key West, the film explores the musicians, friendships, touring years, and studio sessions that helped shape Buffett’s legendary sound. Through rare, never-before-seen archival footage and deeply personal interviews with founding members, tour managers, producers and music legends, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD captures the camaraderie, chaos, and magic of an era that thrived on freedom and lived without a rulebook. Narrated by Academy-award winner Jeff Bridges, OCCUPATIONAL HAZARD offers fans a deeper look at the people behind the music and the era that helped define Jimmy Buffett’s lasting legacy. This film is a tribute to Buffett and the original Coral Reefers, the places and people that shaped them, the volatile beauty of a musical moment that couldn’t last but changed everything and their candid sentiment toward Buffett. It’s the origin story upon which the Parrot Head empire was built upon, by the people who helped lay the foundation.

screenings.title: Soul Patrol
screenings.description: SOUL PATROL uncovers a hidden chapter of American military history by focusing on the Vietnam War’s first Black special ops team, an elite unit operating deep behind enemy lines. With unprecedented access to this once-secretive group of African-American veterans, director J.M. Harper reconstructs their journey with an immediacy rarely seen in Vietnam War storytelling, using raw Super 8 footage, photographs, and audio recordings from their personal archives. Opening on the war’s 50th anniversary, the surviving members reunite in a hotel that becomes a surreal liminal space, where memory, brotherhood, and unresolved trauma collide. As the men reflect on their experiences, the film interrogates the contradictions of fighting for freedom abroad while facing inequality at home. Winner of the Directing Award for U.S. Documentary at the Sundance Film Festival, Soul Patrol is not just a war story, but a reckoning – an intimate portrait of survival, memory, and the enduring cost of war on those asked to fight it.

screenings.title: Pickup on South Street
screenings.description: U.S., 1953 Directed by Samuel Fuller Starring Richard Widmark, Richard Widmark Jean Peters, Thelma Ritter, Richard Kiley, Willis Bouchey, Milburn Stone Approx. 80 min. “Are you waving the flag at me?,” sneers pickpocket Richard Widmark at cops and Feds on the trail of that microfilm he’s lifted on the subway from Jean Peters’ purse—after all, she was messengering it, albeit unwittingly, to the REDS! But then, in Widmark’s world, “Who cares? Your money’s as good as anybody else’s”; while professional snitch Thlema Ritter thoughtfully pulls out a price chart when called on for a fingering. (This was Ritter’s fourth straight Supporting Actress Oscar® nomination—her sixth was for BIRDMAN OF ALCATRAZ; she never won.) Peters herself—soon to be Mrs. Howard Hughes in real life—is everybody’s patsy, blackmailed into the mule deal by sweaty ex-“boyfriend” Richard Kiley with promise of a clean final breakup, robbed twice, cold-cocked, hit with a beer-in-the-face wakeup call, and rag-dolled around an apartment; and shot. But finally, as Ritter says, “Even in our crummy line of business, you gotta draw the line somewhere.” Vintage Fuller hard-boiled pulp, with final chin-bouncing-on-each-step subway station showdown. (Released the year Stalin died, PICKUP’s Cold War attitudes horrified Gallic Fuller fans; in the French dubbing, the whole thing was changed to a drug deal.)

When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.description: “Poetic, political, and above all incontrovertibly material” [The New Yorker], Kogonada’s fourth feature, the experimental drama zi, follows the title character, played by Michelle Mao, a concert violinist whose aimless peregrinations through the streets of Hong Kong are interrupted by visions of what may be either her past or future, a condition she attempts to explain to a new American acquaintance (Haley Lu Richardson, Columbus) while a stranger (Jin Ha) observes the pair from a distance. A valentine to the textures and colors of the Fragrant Harbor as seen by night, featuring music by the late Ryuichi Sakamoto, the formally audacious, shot-on-the-fly zi is a film of unusual delicacy and reserve, one whose air of mystery abides long after the credits have rolled.

Stanley Kubrick’s savage adaptation of Anthony Burgess’s 1962 novel is among the most infamous and controversial mainstream movies ever made. McDowell is unforgettable as Alex, the amoral, nihilist, Beethoven-obsessed head of the Droogs, a gang of marauding teen rapists and murderers rampaging across a dystopic, diseased future London. After arrest, he is subject to a treatment in which his violent impulses are turned back on him, leading to provocative questions about government control and free will. screenings.title: Last Stop for the Circular Ticket
screenings.description: THE THEATER OF THE MATTERS & TAUFIC PRESENT:JEAN-CLAUDE ROUSSEAU’S ‘THE PASTORAL CONCERT’ + ‘LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET’This book launch event celebrates the release of Jean-Claude Rousseau’s unclassifiable, long-unavailable film text, The Pastoral Concert, published for the first time in English this October by Taufic. The evening will culminate in a special premiere screening of Rousseau’s new feature film, LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET (winner of a Jury Special Mention at this year’s FIDMarseille), alongside his 2006 short, FAUX DÉPART.The Pastoral Concert marks the first English translation of Rousseau’s early written work Le Concert champêtre, begun in 1968, some fifteen years before his debut film. Rousseau continued shaping the work as a screenplay until its rejection by the Centre National de la Cinématographie in 1983. Unrealized, Le Concert champêtre became the matrix from which Rousseau’s subsequent films would emerge.Taking its title and three central characters (A, B, and C) from the eponymous painting long attributed to Giorgione and now to Titian, The Pastoral Concert begins as a letter written by a young man to his cousin in the countryside on the eve of her wedding, before mutating into a diary entry, a screenplay, and finally a film imagined through the failure of its own realization. In this restless fluctuation between registers, The Pastoral Concert expresses, in the words of Jean-Marie Straub, “something magnificent [and] entirely different from a screenplay or a découpage.”Translated from the French by artist and filmmaker Kevin Weil, this edition includes an extensive appendix of extra-diegetic materials written by Rousseau, as well as correspondence with contemporaries such as Dominique Noguez, Marcel Hanoun, and Jean-Marie Straub, which form a picture of the work’s early reception.For more info about The Pastoral Concert visit: https://taufic.org/the-pastoral-concertJean-Claude RousseauLAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET / DERNIER ARRÊT POUR LE BILLET CIRCULAIRE2026, 87 min, DCP. No dialogue.Rousseau’s longest film since THE ENCLOSED VALLEY from 1995 (the summit of his 8mm era), LAST STOP FOR THE CIRCULAR TICKET refers to the looped ferry route that plies the waters of Lake Como in Northern Italy. Firmly grounded in place, Rousseau’s solitary camera finds desolate poetry in the void of the spectacular landscape and in the anonymous crowds of passengers seemingly entranced at the edge of an abyss. Musical chords and voices magnify their gestures and the movement of the vessel on the lake. Closing the circle, the specter of the end looms: “On the ferry, among the travelers, I recognized Mrs. Death…”Preceded by:Jean-Claude Rousseau FAUX DÉPART (2006, 13 min, DCP. No dialogue.)CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.description: An essential text for anyone with a love for the avant-garde. The explosive soundscapes of industrial music titans Einstürzende Neubauten first shook Berlin – then the whole world – to its core in the 1980s. In LIEBESLIEDER, co-directors Klaus Maeck and Johanna Schenkel wield a fractured feast of killer Neubauten performances from Euro television: ones that highlight the group’s cinematic presence, wild handmade instruments, and totally unique style. For those who are at all curious about industrial or noise music in general, this sweaty documentary is unmissable. For Neubauten fans, this humanizing portrait of their first decade provides a fresh take on the band.CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

screenings.description: In The Brood, the bitter divorce between the mentally disturbed Nola (Samantha Eggar) and her ex-husband Frank (Art Hindle) was pretty messy, so it should be a good sign that she’s finally getting professional help from the renowned Dr. Hal Raglan (Oliver Reed)—but Frank can’t help but notice that people on Nola’s long list of enemies keep dying at the hands of asexual, dwarfish assassins, and so he starts to wonder what exactly the experimental therapy practiced at Dr. Raglan’s Somafree Institute consists of… Written while Cronenberg was in the midst of his own divorce and custody battle, The Brood is a brutal, bracing airing of anxieties gussied up in grindhouse trappings.

screenings.title: Lost Highway
screenings.description: Few filmmakers have shown themselves so adept at plumbing the depths of the subconscious without coming up for air as Lynch, whose Lost Highway—inspired loosely by still-fresh coverage of the O. J. Simpson trial—begins as a dark domestic drama concerning a sexually incompetent saxophonist (Bill Pullman) and his wife (Patricia Arquette), morphs into a movie about a cocksman mechanic (Balthazar Getty) who gets involved with a gangster’s girl (Arquette, again), and ends with an unleashing of apocalyptic, purgative flame… Whether you take it as a cinematic depiction of a psychogenic fugue state or a free-associative disgorging of images from Hollywood’s id, Lynch’s film has the pull of a whirlpool and the terrible logic of a nightmare.

screenings.title: The Silence of the Lambs
screenings.description: Clarice Starling, a top student at the FBI’s training academy, is sent to interview Dr. Hannibal Lecter, to provide insight into a serial killer being pursued by the FBI. In a now iconic role, Anthony Hopkin’s Lecter is a brilliant psychiatrist who is also a violent psychopath, serving life behind bars for acts of murder and cannibalism. Tense, beautiful and arresting, Jonathan Demme’s The Silence of the Lambs mingles the horrors of criminal acts with the psychological horrors of Lecter’s slow-motion interrogation of Clarice and of her memories that emerge from it.

screenings.title: The Devils
screenings.description: Ken Russell’s controversial adaptation of Aldous Huxley’s The Devils of Loudun is at long last available in its full, provocative splendor. This new restoration thrillingly incorporates material that was originally censored—footage that Russell deemed some of the best and most political work of his career. A young Derek Jarman designed the sets that house this story of a vengeful nun (Vanessa Redgrave) who accuses a priest (Oliver Reed) of collaborating with the devil, resulting in the apparent possession of an entire convent. A fearless account of state and church corruption, The Devils mixes graphic sexual imagery with religious iconography in an unforgettable spectacle that could only issue from the mind of Ken Russell. Following its NYFF64 premiere, The Devils will open on 35mm for a one-week engagement beginning October 16 at Film at Lincoln Center. A Warner Bros. Clockwork release.

screenings.title: Far From Heaven
screenings.description: An homage to the Eisenhower era melodramas of Douglas Sirk that reworks the basic materials of his 1955 All That Heaven Allows to explicitly explore dynamics of sexual and social transgression verboten in the Hollywood of Sirk’s time, Haynes’s sumptuous film—featuring a period-appropriate score by Elmer Bernstein and a remarkable approximation of Technicolor saturation by cinematographer Ed Lachman—stars Julianne Moore and Dennis Quaid as a well-heeled Connecticut couple whose seemingly perfect suburban existence is upended when he’s discovered trawling Hartford’s gay bars and she strikes up an affair with her new Black gardener, played with compassionate gravity by Dennis Haysbert.

screenings.title: The Housemaid
screenings.description: Cited by Bong Joon-ho as an inspiration on his Parasite and widely regarded by South Korean cinephiles and scholars as one of the country’s greatest films, The Housemaid can now be discovered by the rest of the world thanks to a restoration by the Korean Film Archive and Martin Scorsese’s World Cinema Project. The routine domestic life of a middle-class family is turned upside-down after a young woman (Lee Eun-shim) joins the household to help with the chores—though what she does instead is turn the house into a boiling cauldron of lust. A mélange of melodrama, morality tale, noir thriller, and horror film that, in Kim’s handling, come together to exercise a vice-like grip.

screenings.title: Testament with Lynne Littman in person
screenings.description: Followed by a Q&A with director Lynne Littman Dir. Lynne Littman. 1983, 89 mins. U.S. 35mm print courtesy of the Lynne Littman Collection at the Academy Film Archive. With Jane Alexander, William Devane, Roxana Zal, Ross Harris, Lukas Haas, Leon Ames, Kevin Costner, Rebecca DeMornay. No one who has seen Testament has ever forgotten it. Released at the height of the Cold War nuclear scare of the early 1980s, this harrowing, intimate drama stars Jane Alexander, in an Oscar-nominated performance, as a California wife and mother struggling to hold her family together after the unthinkable happens: a nuclear strike on the U.S. Keeping the focus entirely on one household and the tight-knit neighborhood around it, director Lynne Littman fashioned the scariest and subtlest movie about the end of the world in American cinema history. We are pleased to present this underseen masterpiece with director Littman in person. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. screenings.title: Detour
screenings.description: Hearing a certain tune spin on the jukebox in an all-night diner in Reno sends down-on-his-luck pianist Al Roberts (Tom Neal) on a traumatic trip down memory lane, recalling his fateful roadside encounter with Ann Savage’s aptly named femme fatale Vera and his subsequent subjugation to her, in Ulmer’s made-for-peanuts classic of noir absurdism, one of the priceless treasures to emerge from Hollywood’s so-called “Poverty Row” studios. “Possibly the bleakest, most doom-laden film noir ever… Savage’s sensational performance, combined with the real-life trajectory of Neal, who ended up going to prison for murdering his wife, have made this a tormented film with the despairing logic of nightmare.” —The Los Angeles Times

screenings.title: Two Seasons, Two Strangers preceded by Nagahama
screenings.description: Based on two manga by Yoshiharu Tsuge, who rose to underground celebrity thanks to his surrealist tales published in the pages of Garo, the bastion of Japanese avant-garde cartooning, Miyake’s bifurcated live-action feature observes (and draws parallels and contrasts from) a summertime meet-cute between Nagisa and Natsuo (Yuumi Kawai and Mansaku Takada) and a snowbound winter encounter between screenwriter Li and innkeeper Ben-zō (Shim Eun-kyung and Shinichi Tsutsumi). Winner of the Golden Leopard at last year’s Locarno Film Festival, hailed “a true masterpiece” by Shiguéhiko Hasumi, Japan’s greatest living film critic, Two Seasons, Two Strangers is at one and the same time as simple as its straightforward title suggests and immensely, exhilaratingly complex. Preceded by Miyake’s short Nagahama, born of a creative collaboration with dancer and actress Shizuka Ishibashi.

screenings.title: Sloan Showcase: After Yang with Kogonada in person + Verse
screenings.description: EMBODIED TECHNOLOGY With directors Kogonada and Noam Argov in person After Yang. Dir. Kogonada. 2022, 96 mins. With Colin Farrell, Justin H. Min, Jodie Turner-Smith, Haley Lu Richardson, Malea Emma Tjandrawidjaja. When his young daughter’s technosapien companion, the android Yang (Min), malfunctions, Jake (Farrell) must come to terms with what this loss means for his family. Adapted from a short story by Alexander Weinstein, and directed with aesthetic precision and restraint by Kogonada, the director of tender films about interpersonal connection such as Columbus and this year’s Zi, After Yang is a sensitive and visually striking inquiry into what it means to be human. Preceded by Verse. Dir. Noam Argov. 2026, 18 mins. With Taj Cross, Jesse LaTourette, Will Dagger. Seventeen-year-old Adam is forced to confront where his virtual persona ends and his physical self begins when he decides to meet his VR girlfriend in real life. Both of these films have received recognition and/or support from the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation’s program in Public Understanding of Science and Technology. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission. Visitors are encouraged to view the exhibition Overexposed: Art, Technology, and the Body, which can be added on to their film ticket for $2.50. Special Guests: Kogonada is a writer and director. His first feature, Columbus, premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in 2017. Noam Argov is an award-winning writer/director and National Geographic Explorer whose work explores identity and the spaces between worlds. Her 2023 narrative short Sulam (Ladder) premiered in competition at Aspen Shortsfest and won Best U.S. Student Film at Palm Springs ShortFest; her feature screenplay Princess won NYU’s Purple List Table-Read Initiative, where it was staged in its entirety for producers and executives; and her latest short, Verse, received the Sloan Production Award for its exploration of VR and neuroscience and had its world premiere at the 2026 Tribeca Film Festival. Noam is also a producer on Forbidden Fruits (SXSW 2026), starring Lili Reinhart and Lola Tung and released theatrically by IFC, and Punter, a proof-of-concept film executive produced by Spike Lee and a finalist for the Student BAFTA. Sappir Argov is an American actor and writer whose work spans film, podcasting, and live performance. She is a co-writer of Verse. Sappir starred in short films for top-tier MFA programs, including NYU Tisch and UCLA, as well as an independent short screened for producers at Blumhouse. She is also starring in two upcoming projects slated for release in 2026. Her commercial work includes a global travel campaign aired on NBC. In her writing, Sappir’s original podcast Passing Through ranked in the Top 100 narrative comedy shows on Apple Podcasts.

screenings.title: Personal Problems | The Ravishing Cinema of Bill Gunn
screenings.description: What happens when a group of unbankable individuals tell their stories? Actors who have final say over their speaking parts? A director who was found ‘too difficult’ for Hollywood? A composer who would not submit the hack soundtracks required by the industry? A Black male lead who was not Black enough? A Black actress who was not light enough? An actor who had been retired because he belonged to another era? A cinematographer who chose art over expediency? An unmarketable co-actor who didn’t look like Clark Gable or a male version of Vanessa Williams? Two producers, having no experience, had the audacity to organize a production with the amount of money that Hollywood spends on catering? Maybe less.

screenings.title: After Winter Comes Spring
screenings.description: "Shot in luminous black-and-white, Misselwitz’s After Winter Comes Spring travels a German Democratic Republic that very soon will be no more, conversing with women of all ages on stops along the way to create a group portrait of female East Germany—one that interrogates the outgoing leadership’s claims of advancing equality between the genders while looking anxiously towards the new world in the process of being born. “‘At the age of 40 I set out once again from the town of my childhood,’ explains Misselwitz at the start of her railway journey, ‘to discover how others have lived and how they want to live.’ Her film exists in the gap between the two. The women she meets speak plainly of regret, longing, and hope: the teenage runaways, the divorcée split between factory work and caring for her disabled daughter, and the great-grandmother who, after 60 years of marriage, quietly admits it was a mistake to marry her husband.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue"
